description: Count every fielding row (one per player, year, stint and position) for each batting hand.

a.request: Matching fielding records to players on `player_id`, count the fielding records for each batting hand (`player.bats`), treating each value, including blank or missing ones, as its own group. Give each hand's share of the total of those counts. Show only the batting hands whose count is above the average count per hand. For each, list the batting hand, the count, its share, and how far the count is above that average, unrounded and in no particular order.
a.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT p.bats AS bats, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fielding f JOIN player p ON p.player_id = f.player_id GROUP BY p.bats), total AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt, AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM counts) SELECT c.bats AS bats, c.cnt AS cnt, c.cnt * 1.0 / t.total_cnt AS share, c.cnt - t.avg_cnt AS above_avg FROM counts c CROSS JOIN total t WHERE c.cnt > t.avg_cnt;

b.request: Count every fielding row (each player, year, stint, and position) grouped by `player.bats`, with NULL or blank hands as their own groups, then report each hand's share of total fielding rows and keep only the hands whose count exceeds the average count across hands, showing the unrounded excess over that average
b.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT CASE WHEN p.bats IS NULL THEN 'NULL' WHEN TRIM(p.bats) = '' THEN 'BLANK' ELSE TRIM(p.bats) END AS hand FROM fielding fl LEFT JOIN player p ON p.player_id = fl.player_id), g AS (SELECT hand, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM f GROUP BY hand), t AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT g.hand, g.cnt, g.cnt * 1.0 / t.total AS share, g.cnt - t.avg_cnt AS excess_over_avg FROM g CROSS JOIN t WHERE g.cnt > t.avg_cnt;

c.request: Break fielding down by batting hand: match fielding to players on `player_id` and give the fielding count for each batting hand (`player.bats`), with blank or missing hands as their own groups. Give each hand's share of the total. Keep only the hands whose count is above the average across hands. For each, show the batting hand, the count, the share, and how far the count is above that average, unrounded. Count every fielding row (one per player, year, stint and position) for each batting hand.
c.sql: WITH hand_counts AS (SELECT p.bats AS batting_hand, COUNT(*) AS fielding_count FROM fielding f JOIN player p ON p.player_id = f.player_id GROUP BY p.bats), totals AS (SELECT SUM(fielding_count) AS total_count, AVG(fielding_count) AS avg_count FROM hand_counts) SELECT h.batting_hand, h.fielding_count, CAST(h.fielding_count AS REAL) / t.total_count AS share, h.fielding_count - t.avg_count AS above_average FROM hand_counts h CROSS JOIN totals t WHERE h.fielding_count > t.avg_count;

d.request:
Rephrase the follow-up as a standalone question:

"For each batting hand (`player.bats`), count every fielding row (one per player, year, stint, and position), treating blank or missing hands as their own groups."
d.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN p.bats IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN TRIM(p.bats) = '' THEN 'blank' ELSE p.bats END AS bats, COUNT(*) AS fielding_rows FROM fielding f LEFT JOIN player p ON p.player_id = f.player_id GROUP BY 1;
